note: Attacker-controlled second ftyp box at the file container level is accepted because avifParse never enforces uniqueness of ftyp boxes. avifRWDataSet reallocates data->ftypData to a different size (12 -> 4), which frees the old buffer that data->ftyp.compatibleBrands (set by the first ftyp box) still points into.

The CHECK macro returns AVIF_FALSE (== 0 == AVIF_RESULT_OK) when avifParseFileTypeBox fails, so the truncated second ftyp's parse error is masked: avifParse returns success even though ftyp was only partially updated and ftyp.compatibleBrands is left dangling.

The truncated second ftyp box (12-byte box: header + 4-byte majorBrand only) fails the minorVersion read and this check before ftyp->compatibleBrands / ftyp->compatibleBrandsCount are refreshed, so the stale pointer into the freed ftypData buffer survives together with the old count of 1.

Because avifParse returned AVIF_RESULT_OK despite the masked failure, parsing continues and the corrupted avifFileType (dangling compatibleBrands, count 1, majorBrand now 'XXXX') is handed to the compatibility check.

majorBrand is 'XXXX' (neither avif nor avis), so the loop over compatibleBrandsCount executes and memcmp dereferences ftyp->compatibleBrands, which points into the freed ftypData buffer -> heap-use-after-free read of 4 bytes.
